3.1.8.value:
Zero data retention by default: model inputs and outputs are not stored by default (synchronous inference); for async inference, inputs are stored only temporarily until processed and outputs are never stored
Per-customer dedicated Kubernetes namespace with workload isolation enforced through Calico and Cilium; nodes run in private subnets with firewall protections
Annual penetration testing by independent third-party security firms; malicious model deployments tested in a dedicated prod-like environment
Encrypted secrets storage scoped to the customer workspace; secrets encrypted and injected into the model environment only at runtime
SSO via SAML 2.0 with major identity providers (Okta, Google Workspace, Azure AD) plus SCIM 2.0 directory sync; role-based access control on workspaces; scoped workspace/personal API keys with central admin revocation
Single-tenant, self-hosted, and hybrid deployment options that keep workloads and data in the customer's own cloud
Regional environments that route inference traffic exclusively to workload planes within a designated geographic region (US, EU, UK, Australia), guaranteeing data stays in the designated region
SOC 2 Type II certified and HIPAA compliant (both Baseten-hosted and self-hosted deployments)
3.1.8.locator: Assembled one-per-line from: docs.baseten.co/observability/security (zero data retention, Kubernetes namespace isolation via Calico/Cilium, private subnets/firewalls, annual third-party penetration testing, SOC 2 Type II + HIPAA), docs.baseten.co/organization/secrets (encrypted secrets), baseten.co/resources/changelog/sso-and-scim/ and docs.baseten.co/observability/access (SSO/SAML 2.0, SCIM, RBAC, API key management), baseten.co/deployments/baseten-self-hosted/ and /baseten-hybrid/ (single-tenant/self-hosted/hybrid), docs.baseten.co/deployment/regional-environments (region-locked routing)
3.1.8.notes: Every line traces to a baseten.co or docs.baseten.co page surfaced in domain-restricted search snippets this session; none of the pages could be fetched directly (gateway EGRESS_BLOCKED). Deliberately excludes anything only claimed by third parties or inferable from the underlying cloud providers Baseten runs on. | Corroborated/detailed by Baseten Labs, Inc. open_questions_for_vendor: Please confirm the exact legal entity that contracts for the Baseten service (full name, legal form, and state of incorporation — is it Baseten Labs, Inc., a Delaware corporation?) and the current registered address (your Terms state 201 Spear Street, Suite 1600, San Francisco, CA 94105).
Has Baseten designated a representative in the EU under Article 27 GDPR? If yes, please provide the representative's name and full address.

Does Baseten have a formally appointed Data Protection Officer? If yes, please provide name, telephone number and/or email; if not, please confirm privacy@baseten.co as the contact entitled to respond to data-protection requests, and provide a telephone number if available.

What minimum TLS version is enforced for data in transit on Baseten inference and management endpoints (TLS 1.2 or 1.3), and is TLS also enforced for internal traffic between platform services and model pods?

Is customer data at rest (async inference inputs while queued, logs, secrets, custom model weights and source code) encrypted, with which algorithm (e.g. AES-256), and on which underlying cloud provider(s)?
Are backups of customer data taken, and if so are they encrypted and with which algorithm?

Who generates and manages the encryption keys for data at rest — Baseten/its cloud provider (shared or customer-specific keys), or can customers supply their own keys (CMEK/BYOK)? Please answer for the Baseten Cloud deployment model specifically.
Can Baseten anonymize and/or pseudonymize customer personal data on the customer's documented instruction (Art. 28(3)(e) GDPR support)?
Beyond SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA, does Baseten hold any of: ISO/IEC 27001, 27018, 27701, 9001, ISO 22301/BS 25999, SOC 1, SOC 3? Please provide current certificates/reports.

For the EU regional environment: does it cover the video/audio inference workloads Tavus runs on Baseten, does it guarantee both processing and storage stay in the EU/EEA, and what is required to enable it for our account?
